steps.text: Mix together flour, cornmeal, milk, egg, sugar, oil, baking powder, and salt in a microwave-safe glass or ceramic bowl until well combined.
Heat in the microwave on high until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 3 minutes. Rotate the bowl halfway through cooking if the microwave does not have a turntable.

raw_recipe.headline: 5 Minute Microwave Cornbread
raw_recipe.description: This microwave cornbread is made with basic pantry ingredients in one bowl and will be on your dinner table in just 5 quick minutes. You'll be amazed!
raw_recipe.name: 5 Minute Microwave Cornbread

review.reviewBody: Decided at the last minute to make cornbread with the chili tonight so I came to allrecipes.com to find a recipe......and I found this one. Since it was the first time making it, I didn't change anything. The hubby said it could be sweeter. I eat mine with butter and honey so I didn't notice. Even the kids liked it. I loved how easy and quick it was to make....and in the microwave. I'd never heard of cornbread done in the microwave before. Mine took a total of six minutes to be completely done but even at that.....it's a heck of a lot shorter than in the oven! And great for a last minute add to dinner! You definitely have to try this!

My husband said this is the best cornbread he's had in his life, and he's 60. He liked it because it was moist inside, but I found it to be firm as well. It didn't crumble to pieces when I split the slices to butter them. The only changes were that I used 3 Tbsp sugar due to previous reviewers advice, and 1/2 tsp salt because salt enhances other flavors. I used a 9" pie plate with a juice glass in the center to ensure against a soggy middle. I greased the cookware, added the batter, and cooked in a 1200 watt microwave for 3 & 1/2 minutes. I reheated it later for 30 seconds with no discernable change in quality.

Let’s face reality, this is a convenience recipe…and a very good one. It will not replace the texture and flavor profile you get from using the traditional methods. I recommend making two small changes; Use butter instead of oil and after the 3 mins. in the microwave cook it 1-2 additional mins. under a toaster (both sides). You will still save time and get a quality result. P.S. mine is going in black-eyed peas or chili anyway. Good Luck!

As a **microwave** cornbread, I'm giving this five stars. I followed the recipe exactly, but added canned sweet corn (because that's how I like my cornbread). It was definitely better than the second batch that did not have any whole corn. I also cooked it in a silicone "Bundt" pan & was very happy with the result -- cooked very evenly & easy to cut into equal pieces. Thanks for this time-saving, yummy recipe! Update: Added >1/2 can of corn this evening vs. a few lg. spoonfuls. The cooking time had to be increased, but the result definitely improved. Very moist. YUM!
so easy to make and so good. instead of sugar I added a half cup of sugar-free honey. also added chopped jalapenos. was spicy sweet. I cooked in oven for 20 min.

Not the prettiest pic , I know. I did this same recipe with TENDA cornbread mix. I only added milk, eggs, oil and sugar to the same proportion of cornmeal mix i.e 1 cup. I used a glass loaf pan so I think that’s why it cooked slower. After 3 mins the center was wet, so added another minute. When it was done I broiled the top( a bit too much this time lol) for color. Finally I added butter to the top. I’ve made many microwave cornbreads and I always recommend broiling the top, even in a toaster oven. It taste and looks better. This recipe is versatile

I made cornbread by experimenting in a mug by using a box of Jiffy cornbread mix in the little blue box. Mix according to directions. Spray the 'over sized coffee mug' with nonstick, pour half the mixture in each mug. Cook one mug at a time for 3 minutes. It did rise above the mug, then it started going back down. Of course it depends on the different microwaves, but now that I have made two of them I will do it for the entire 3 minutes because it dries out the cornbread better making it more like oven baked. Next time I'll try adding jalapeno ;-) for more flavor.

This was surprisingly good and definitely fast! The only thing I did differently was to mix it in a GLASS PIE PLATE and then after cooking in the microwave for three minutes, I turned the oven on BROIL and BROWNED the top of the cornbread just a little. I brushed butter over the top, cut it into wedges, and served it with honey. I still can't believe how fast and easy this was and I'll definitely be making it again when time is short. Thanks for the recipe!

Made this doubled (as I needed a normal recipe amount and this seems like a 1/2 size recipe), added extra sugar and salt.... cooked in a 9 inch square glass baking pan. It took 10 min. in my very old lower wattage microwave, for the doubled batch. Nice consistency, good flavor.... my dead oven problem was evaded. Supper saved. After all, what's a good pot of pinto beans without cornbread?

For someone who loves cornbread and makes homemade cornbread frequently, I was really impressed with the results this recipe achieved in the microwave! While it’s not the same as oven baked, it’s way closer than I had expected. I made some very minor modifications to my own liking - used butter instead of veg oil, coconut/almond creamer as I did not have milk, omitted sugar, and used a scant more cornmeal than flour. I would do this again when short on time. Nice option to have!

First, I easily veganized this recipe by using soy milk and a chia seed egg. I also added some canned corn because I like corn in my cornbread, and I added a half tablespoon more of sugar because I like mine on the sweeter side. Instead of vegetable oil, I used earth balance "butter". I sprinkled a bit more sugar over the top before I microwaved it. My cornbread was ready in 4 minutes, and I ate it with chili or with apricot jam. I didn't mind the texture, and it tasted good to me. It's perfect when you're pressed for time.
Super easy in a pinch… last minute decision to make corn bread for my chili. Very happy with the results!!😄
This had terrible texture… I thought I could do this quickly for lunch with leftover beans & thanksgiving ham. Nope. 👎🏼 One bite & gave the rest to the dogs on their dinner.

I have been reduced to a room in my apartment and have to come up with genius ways to cook my food in a small space. Microwaved on high for 5 minutes total. This came out light and fluffy (not brown) and I stuck it in my air-fryer to put some color and crunch on it ;D I will definitely be using this recipe again and again. I also don't like to cook much anymore so I am all for quick, convenient and tastes great!!

Just finished making this as directed. Came out great. No, it is not the pretty cornbread that you would get in the regular oven, but my intention will be to use it for croutons in salad tomorrow. I think that will be fine.
Once I let it cool some it firmed up nicely.

This is really good for a microwave quick cornbread. My oven has been down for a while, and we wanted cornbread with our chili. It was good enough that I'll make it again! This recipe is basically half the recipe on the back of my cornmeal package, so I just made the full recipe and baked for 5 minutes. I'm so happy to have found this!

We tried this when our oven was being delivered. It's a no go for our southern household, the texture is wrong, the crispy edge from the cast iron rubbed with bacon grease is missing. Instead of faking cornbread in the microwave, we opt for stove top hoe cakes.

This microwave cornbread recipe is amazing; it really only takes 3 minutes to cook … wow!!! I could not believe it! Has great flavor and is moist. My granddaughter and I made it a few minutes ago, and it was so easy to do. I used a 9 x 9 glass pan initially then we doubled the recipe and switched to a larger glass dish, deciding to add 1/8 cup honey to this second batch of batter, cooking the larger second batch 5 minutes 30 seconds. Delicious with or without the honey added! Recipe is a keeper!
Easy and tasty!
